questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses CKAD fundamentals, including CronJobs, PVCs, ConfigMaps, InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, and NetworkPolicies within a realistic risk-based scenario.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and backoff management
- PVC-mounted configuration discovery
- YAML validation with yq for key extraction
- InitContainers for tool installation and sidecar patterns
- Secrets management and TLS certificate rotation
- Namespace-level network policy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-scan
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 0 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: yq-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.35.1/yq_linux_amd64
              chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmap -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o yaml | yq e '.data | keys' - | grep -v '^---\|config.json' && echo "$cm"
              done | curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d @- http://config-scan-portal:8080/api/v1/scan
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: config-scan-secret
                  key: api-key
            volumeMounts:
            - name: configs
              mountPath: /configs
          - name: tls-sidecar
            image: nginx:alpine
            ports:
            - containerPort: 443
              name: https
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/certs
              readOnly: true
          volumes:
          - name: configs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: config-scan-pvc
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: tls-certs
            secret:
              secretName: config-scan-tls
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-scan-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadOnlyMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-scan-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-scan-network-policy
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      job-name: config-scan
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: config-scan-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap listing**: Using a PVC requires storage provisioning but allows scanning ConfigMap YAML files directly. Listing ConfigMaps via kubectl is simpler but lacks filesystem semantics.
- **InitContainer vs sidecar image**: InitContainer adds startup latency but ensures a minimal base scanner image. A custom image with yq pre-installed reduces complexity but increases maintenance.
- **NetworkPolicy granularity**: Restricting egress improves security but may break if the target service endpoint changes. Consider DNS-based policies for flexibility.
- **Probes on sidecar**: Adding probes assumes the sidecar exposes health endpoints; this adds configuration overhead but enables reliable deployment in production clusters.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives (PVC, ConfigMap, Secret) with a small in-cluster data-processor and external API communication.

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: configs
          persistentVolumeClaim:

```

Why This Is Asked
- Tests knowledge of per-namespace tooling with standard CKAD primitives (PVCs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, sidecars, probes, NetworkPolicy).
- Exercises end-to-end flow: manifest reading, batching, external POST, and secure networking.

Key Concepts
- InitContainer installation of scanners
- PVC-mounted manifests and ConfigMap-driven batching
- Secret-based credentials and TLS rotation sidecar
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy
- Minimal YAML skeleton and trade-offs between latency and throughput

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-scan-guardian
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-scan-guardian
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-scan-guardian
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: scanner
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do sleep 60; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /images
              name: images
        - name: main
          image: busybox:1.36
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo running; sleep 3600"]
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:

      initContainers:
        - name: install-scanner
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache --update curl jq && echo scanner installed"]
      volumes:
        - name: images
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: images-pvc
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: reg secret
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle partial failures in batch processing?
- What RBAC changes are appropriate for this per-namespace task?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical lifecycle management and how probes interact with rolling updates to avoid downtime.

## Key Concepts

- StartupProbe, readinessProbe, livenessProbe
- preStop and terminationGracePeriodSeconds
- Graceful shutdown patterns in Node.js apps

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-server
  namespace: prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-server
        image: node:18
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          failureThreshold: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 15
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["bash","-lc","sleep 5"]
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust thresholds for busy traffic?
- How would you verify graceful shutdown under load?
- What pitfalls exist with preStop sleeps in container runtimes?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical RBAC auditing skills within the CKAD scope, including multi-namespace governance, secure logging, and egress constraints.

## Key Concepts

- **RBAC objects**: RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings, and ServiceAccounts at the namespace level
- **ConfigMap-driven policy**: External policy reference for audit rules
- **Namespace-scoped auditing**: Decentralized audit model vs. cluster-wide approaches
- **Pod lifecycle**: InitContainers for tool installation, readiness/liveness probes for reliability
- **Storage**: PVC-backed logging at /logs
- **Network security**: Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting egress to the audit endpoint

## Trade-offs

- **Pros**: Decentralized scaling, namespace isolation, ConfigMap flexibility for policy updates
- **Cons**: Resource overhead per namespace, potential for policy drift, Secret management complexity, duplicated effort across namespaces

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rbac-policy
data:
  policy.yaml: |-
    allowedBindings:
      - kind: User
        name: admin
    maxServiceAccounts: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-token: <token>
  endpoint: https://audit.example.com/api/v1/digest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: rbac-auditor
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rbac-auditor
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - "wget -qO /tools/curl https://curl.se/download && wget -qO /tools/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /tools/*"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: alpine:latest
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache curl jq
              while true; do
                kubectl get rolebindings,clusterrolebindings,serviceaccounts -o json > /logs/snapshot.json
                curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @/logs/snapshot.json $ENDPOINT
                sleep 3600
              done
          env:
            - name: TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: bearer-token
            - name: ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: audit-credentials
                  key: endpoint
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-logs
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: target-ns
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rbac-auditor
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: audit-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-resource-guard
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: ns-resource-guard-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq && echo done"]
          containers:
          - name: guard
            image: bitnami/kubectl:1.28
            command: ["sh", "-c", "kubectl get deploy --all-namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.requests==null or .spec.template.spec.containers[]?.resources?.limits==null) | .metadata.namespace' | sort -u | while read ns; do kubectl -n $ns patch deploy --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources","value": {"requests": {"cpu":"100m","memory":"128Mi"}, "limits": {"cpu":"200m","memory":"256Mi"}}}]' || true; done"]
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: defaults
            configMap:
              name: resource-defaults
          tolerations:
          - operator: Exists
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

```javascript
# Minimal skeleton for a Deployment that performs config sync
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-sync
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-sync

      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for tooling setup
- PVC mounting and data direction between /data/events and /data/enriched
- ConfigMap/Secret for runtime config and credentials
- TLS sidecar for certificate rotation
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy for scoped egress
- Load testing and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-config
data:
  batchSize: "100"
  enrichmentEndpoint: "http://enrich-controller.analytics.svc.cluster.local:8080/enrich"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  apiToken: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myrepo/config-aggregator:latest
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: config-aggregator-config
            - secretRef:
                name: config-aggregator-creds
          volumeMounts:
            - name: events
              mountPath: /data/events
            - name: enriched
              mountPath: /data/enriched
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: events
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-events-pvc
        - name: enriched
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-enriched-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace isolation across multiple environments?
- What scaling considerations arise with batchSize tuning and backpressure?
- How would you observe and debug under intermittent enrichment endpoint failures?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks secure defaults and practical CKAD patterns: ConfigMap/Secret usage, correct SecurityContext, and health checks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities: drop: ALL
- ConfigMap and Secret mounting into containers
- Resource requests/limits
- Liveness and readiness probes
- ClusterIP service exposure

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flask-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flask-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flask-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: flask
        image: python:3.11-slim
        command: ["python", "/app/main.py"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-config
          mountPath: /app/config
        - name: api-key
          mountPath: /secrets
          readOnly: true
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 1001
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      volumes:
      - name: app-config
        configMap:
          name: flask-config
      - name: api-key
        secret:
          secretName: flask-api-key
```

```yaml
# Minimal Service skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: flask-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: flask-app
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 5000
  type: ClusterIP
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the API_KEY secret without downtime?
- What are the trade-offs of using readOnlyRootFilesystem in production?
